findings.lens: charismatic non-denominational (Vineyard, Bethel, Hillsong, Third Wave)
findings.claim: An axis named 'Kingdom' lists no kingdom-present passage; charismatics reach first for Matthew 12:28 and Matthew 6:10.
findings.evidence: key_passages: Romans 11, Galatians 3, Revelation 20, Daniel 9, 1 Thessalonians 4, Matthew 24, Ephesians 2. Bethel's whole program is Matthew 6:10 'on earth as it is in heaven' (Johnson, When Heaven Invades Earth); Vineyard's is Matthew 12:28 / Luke 4:18-19 / Mark 1:15.

findings.claim: The passage list contains no Old Testament covenant text, though the whole dispensational case rests on the Abrahamic and Davidic covenants read in the prophets.
findings.evidence: Listed: Romans 11, Galatians 3:26–29, Revelation 20:1–6, Daniel 9:24–27, 1 Thessalonians 4:13–17, Matthew 24, Ephesians 2:11–22. Galatians 3 and Ephesians 2 are the covenantal proof texts; only Daniel 9 and 1 Thessalonians 4 are distinctly ours, and both concern the tribulation/rapture, not Israel's promises. Every standard dispensational treatment begins from Genesis 12:1–3; 15:18–21; 17:7–8, 2 Samuel 7:12–16, Jeremiah 31:31–37 (note vv. 35–37 on Israel's permanence) and Acts 1:6–7 (Pentecost, Things to Come, chs. 4–8; Walvoord, The Millennial Kingdom, chs. 12–15). Romans 11 should be pointed at 11:25–29 ('the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable').
findings.fix: Replace 'Matthew 24' with 'Genesis 12:1–3; 15:18–21' and add 'Jeremiah 31:31–37' and 'Acts 1:6–7'; narrow 'Romans 11' to 'Romans 11:25–29'. If the axis keeps its millennial framing, Revelation 20:1–6 stays; otherwise it belongs to a millennium item.

findings.lens: Presbyterian / Reformed (Westminster Standards, Three Forms of Unity)
findings.claim: Galatians 3:16 and Hebrews 8:6-13 are the covenantal texts the dispensationalist debate actually turns on and are absent, while Daniel 9 and 1 Thessalonians 4 (dispensational) are present.
findings.evidence: Horton and Riddlebarger (the left read-more) both argue from Galatians 3:16 (the seed is Christ) and Hebrews 8 (the new covenant promised to Israel is fulfilled in the church).

findings.claim: The dispensational pole is represented only by eschatological timetable texts (Daniel 9:24-27, 1 Thessalonians 4:13-17) and has none of the Abrahamic covenant passages on which dispensationalism actually rests: the unconditional, 'everlasting' land promise of Genesis 12:1-3; 15:18-21; 17:7-8 is what statement 10 ("promises to national Israel will be fulfilled literally") means. The covenantal pole lacks its new-covenant text, Hebrews 8:6-13 (quoting Jeremiah 31:31-34), where a covenant made 'with the house of Israel' is applied to the church, and Galatians 6:16, 'the Israel of God', the phrase behind statement 11's "the church is the true Israel".
findings.evidence: Ryrie, Dispensationalism (in read_more), ch. 8, and Walvoord, The Millennial Kingdom, ch. 12-13, ground the Israel-church distinction on the unconditional Abrahamic covenant of Genesis 12, 15, 17; Scofield's notes on Genesis 12:1 and 15:18 do the same. Horton, Introducing Covenant Theology (in read_more), ch. 3-4, and Riddlebarger, A Case for Amillennialism, ch. 4, argue one people of God from Jeremiah 31/Hebrews 8 and Galatians 6:16.
findings.fix: Add "Genesis 17:7–8" (dispensational; or "Genesis 12:1–3") and "Hebrews 8:6–13" (covenantal); if space allows, also "Galatians 6:16". Resulting list: "Genesis 17:7–8", "Romans 11", "Galatians 3:26–29", "Hebrews 8:6–13", "Ephesians 2:11–22", "Daniel 9:24–27", "Revelation 20:1–6", "1 Thessalonians 4:13–18", "Matthew 24".

findings.claim: "1 Thessalonians 4:13–17" stops one verse short of the unit; v.18, 'Therefore encourage one another with these words', closes the paragraph in every standard edition, and the pastoral purpose clause is part of what both pretribulational and posttribulational readers argue from.
findings.evidence: NA28 paragraphing 1 Thess 4:13-18; ESV/NIV/NRSV heading 'The Coming of the Lord' 4:13-18; Ryrie, Blaising & Bock and Ladd all cite 4:13-18.
